readings.title: The Dreams of the Cupbearer and Baker
readings.subtitle: Joseph Interprets the Visions
readings.text:
[Genesis 40:1] And after these events it came to be that the cupbearer and the baker of the sovereign of Mitsrayim sinned against their master, the sovereign of Mitsrayim.
[2] And Pharaoh was wroth with his two officers, the chief cupbearer and the chief baker.
[3] So he put <dn>את</dn> them in confinement in the house of the captain of the guard, in the prison, the place where Yosěph was a prisoner.
[4] And the captain of the guard put <dn>את</dn> Yosěph in charge of them, and he served <dn>את</dn> them. So they were in confinement for some time.
[5] Then the cupbearer and the baker of the sovereign of Mitsrayim, who were confined in the prison, dreamed a dream, both of them, each man’s dream in one night and each man’s dream with its own interpretation.
[6] And Yosěph came in to them in the morning and looked at <dn>את</dn> them and saw that they were sad.
[7] And he asked <dn>את</dn> Pharaoh’s officers who were with him in confinement of his master’s house, saying, “Why do you look so sad today?”
[8] And they said to him, “We each have dreamed a dream, and there is no one to interpret it.” And Yosěph said to them, “Do not interpretations belong to <dn>Elohim</dn>? Relate them to me, please.”
[9] So the chief cupbearer related <dn>את</dn> his dream to Yosěph, and said to him, “See, in my dream a vine was before me,
[10] and in the vine were three branches, and it was as though it budded – its blossoms shot forth, and its clusters brought forth ripe grapes.
[11] “And Pharaoh’s cup was in my hand. So I took <dn>את</dn> the grapes and pressed <dn>את</dn> them into Pharaoh’s cup, and placed <dn>את</dn> the cup in Pharaoh’s hand.”
[12] And Yosěph said to him, “This is the interpretation of it: The three branches are three days.
[13] “Yet, within three days Pharaoh is going to lift up <dn>את</dn> your head and restore you to your place, and you shall put Pharaoh’s cup in his hand according to the former ruling, when you were his cupbearer.
[14] “But remember me when it is well with you, and please show loving-commitment to me. And mention me to Pharaoh, and get me out of this house.
[15] “For truly I was stolen away from the land of the Hebrews. And also I have done naught that they should put me into the dungeon.”
[16] And the chief baker saw that the interpretation was good, and he said to Yosěph, “I also was in my dream and saw three white baskets were on my head,
[17] and in the uppermost basket all kinds of baked goods for Pharaoh, and the birds ate <dn>את</dn> them out of the basket on my head.”
[18] And Yosěph answered and said, “This is the interpretation of it: The three baskets are three days.
[19] “Yet, within three days Pharaoh is going to lift off <dn>את</dn> your head from you and hang <dn>את</dn> you on a tree. And the birds shall eat <dn>את</dn> your flesh from you.”
[20] And on the third day, Pharaoh’s birthday, it came to be that he made a feast for all his servants. And he lifted up <dn>את</dn> the head of the chief cupbearer and <dn>את</dn> of the chief baker among his servants,
[21] and he restored <dn>את</dn> the chief cupbearer to his post of cupbearer again, and he placed the cup in Pharaoh’s hand,
[22] but he hanged <dn>את</dn> the chief baker, as Yosěph had interpreted to them.
[23] And the chief cupbearer did not remember <dn>את</dn> Yosěph, but forgot him.

readings.title: The Altar at Bethel
readings.subtitle: God Blesses Jacob
readings.text:
[Genesis 35:1] And <dn>Elohim</dn> said to Ya‛aqoḇ, <dq>“Arise, go up to Běyth Ěl and dwell there. And make a slaughter-place there to <dn>Ěl</dn> who appeared to you when you fled from the face of Ěsav your brother.”</dq>
[2] And Ya‛aqoḇ said to his household and to all who were with him, “Put away <dn>את</dn> the foreign mighty ones that are among you, and cleanse yourselves, and change your garments.
[3] “And let us arise and go up to Běyth Ěl, and let me make there a slaughter-place to <dn>Ěl</dn>, who answered <dn>את</dn> me in the day of my distress, and has been with me in the way which I have gone.”
[4] So they gave Ya‛aqoḇ <dn>את</dn> all the foreign mighty ones which were in their hands, and <dn>את</dn> all their earrings which were in their ears. And Ya‛aqoḇ hid <dn>את</dn> them under the terebinth tree which was near Sheḵem.
[5] And they departed, and the fear of <dn>Elohim</dn> was upon the cities that were all around them, and they did not pursue the sons of Ya‛aqoḇ.
[6] And Ya‛aqoḇ came to Luz, that is Běyth Ěl, which is in the land of Kena‛an, he and all the people who were with him.
[7] And he built there a slaughter-place and called the place El Běyth Ěl, because there <dn>Elohim</dn> appeared to him when he fled from the face of his brother.
[8] And Deḇorah, Riḇqah’s nurse, died, and she was buried below Běyth Ěl under the terebinth tree. So the name of it was called Allon Baḵuth.
[9] And <dn>Elohim</dn> appeared to Ya‛aqoḇ again, when he came from Paddan Aram, and blessed <dn>את</dn> him.
[10] And <dn>Elohim</dn> said to him, <dq>“Your name is Ya‛aqoḇ, your name is no longer called Ya‛aqoḇ, but Yisra’ěl is your name.”</dq> So <dn>He</dn> called <dn>את</dn> his name Yisra’ěl.
[11] And <dn>Elohim</dn> said to him, <dq>“<dn>I</dn> am <dn>Ěl</dn> Shaddai. Be fruitful and increase, a nation and a company of nations shall be from you, and sovereigns come from your body.</dq>
[12] <dq>“And <dn>את</dn> the land which <dn>I</dn> gave Aḇraham and Yitsḥaq <dn>I</dn> give to you. And to your seed after you <dn>I</dn> give <dn>את</dn> this land.”</dq>
[13] And <dn>Elohim</dn> went up from him in the place where <dn>He</dn> had spoken with <dn>את</dn> him.
[14] And Ya‛aqoḇ set up a standing column in the place where <dn>He</dn> had spoken with <dn>את</dn> him, a monument of stone. And he poured a drink offering on it, and he poured oil on it.
[15] And Ya‛aqoḇ called <dn>את</dn> the name of the place where <dn>Elohim</dn> spoke with <dn>את</dn> him, Běyth Ěl.

readings.title: The Birth of Benjamin and Death of Rachel
readings.subtitle: The Twelve Sons of Israel
readings.text:
[Genesis 35:16] Then they set out from Běyth Ěl. And it came to be, when there was but a little distance to go to Ephrath, that Raḥěl began to give birth, and had great difficulty giving birth.
[17] And it came to be, as she was having great difficulty giving birth, that the midwife said to her, “Do not fear, for it is another son for you.”
[18] And it came to be, as her life was going out – for she died – that she called his name Ben-Oni. But his father called him Binyamin.
[19] So Raḥěl died and was buried on the way to Ephrath, that is Běyth Leḥem.
[20] And Ya‛aqoḇ set a standing column on her burial-place, which is the monument of Raḥěl’s burial-place to this day.
[21] And Yisra’ěl set out and pitched his tent beyond the tower of Ěḏer.
[22] And it came to be, when Yisra’ěl dwelt in that land, that Re’uḇěn went and lay with <dn>את</dn> Bilhah his father’s concubine. And Yisra’ěl heard about it. Now the sons of Ya‛aqoḇ were twelve:
[23] the sons of Lě’ah were Re’uḇěn, Ya‛aqoḇ’s first-born, and Shim‛on, and Lěvi, and Yehuḏah, and Yissasḵar, and Zeḇulun;
[24] the sons of Raḥěl were Yosěph and Binyamin;
[25] the sons of Bilhah, Raḥěl’s female servant, were Dan and Naphtali;
[26] and the sons of Zilpah, Lě’ah’s female servant, were Gaḏ and Ashěr. These were the sons of Ya‛aqoḇ who were born to him in Paddan Aram.

readings.title: The Death of Isaac
readings.subtitle: Gathered to His People
readings.text:
[Genesis 35:27] And Ya‛aqoḇ came to his father Yitsḥaq at Mamrě, or Qiryath Arba, that is Ḥeḇron, where Aḇraham and Yitsḥaq had dwelt.
[28] And the days of Yitsḥaq were one hundred and eighty years.
[29] So Yitsḥaq breathed his last and died, and was gathered to his people, aged and satisfied of days. And his sons Ěsav and Ya‛aqoḇ buried <dn>את</dn> him.

readings.title: Pharaoh's Dreams
readings.subtitle: The Seven Years of Plenty and Famine
readings.text:
[Genesis 41:1] And it came to be, at the end of two years’ time, that Pharaoh had a dream, and saw him standing by the river,
[2] and saw seven cows coming up out of the river, beautiful looking and fat, and they fed amongst the reeds,
[3] then saw seven other cows coming up after them out of the river, ugly and lean of flesh, and stood by the other cows on the bank of the river.
[4] And the ugly and lean of flesh cows ate up <dn>את</dn> the seven beautiful looking and fat cows. Then Pharaoh awoke.
[5] And he slept and dreamed a second time and saw seven heads of grain coming up on one stalk, plump and good,
[6] and saw seven lean heads, scorched by the east wind, coming up after them.
[7] And the seven lean heads swallowed <dn>את</dn> the seven plump and complete heads. Then Pharaoh awoke and saw it was a dream.
[8] And it came to be in the morning that his spirit was moved, and he sent and called for <dn>את</dn> all the magicians of Mitsrayim and <dn>את</dn> all its wise men. And Pharaoh related to them <dn>את</dn> his dreams, but there was no one who could interpret <dn>את</dn> them for Pharaoh.
[9] Then the chief cupbearer spoke to <dn>את</dn> Pharaoh, saying, “I remember <dn>את</dn> my crimes this day.
[10] “When Pharaoh was wroth with his servants, and put <dn>את</dn> me in confinement in the house of the captain of the guard, both <dn>את</dn> me and <dn>את</dn> the chief baker,
[11] each one of us dreamed a dream in one night, he and I. Each of us dreamed according to the interpretation of his own dream.
[12] “And there was with us a Hebrew youth, a servant of the captain of the guard. And we related to him, and he interpreted <dn>את</dn> our dreams for us. To each man he interpreted according to his own dream.
[13] “And it came to be, as he interpreted for us, so it came to be. He restored <dn>את</dn> me to my office, and he hanged <dn>את</dn> him.”
[14] Then Pharaoh sent and called <dn>את</dn> Yosěph, and they hurriedly brought him out of the dungeon. And he shaved and changed his garments, and came to Pharaoh.
[15] And Pharaoh said to Yosěph, “I have dreamed a dream, and there is no one to interpret <dn>את</dn> it. Now I myself have heard it said of you that you understand a dream, to interpret <dn>את</dn> it.”
[16] And Yosěph answered <dn>את</dn> Pharaoh, saying, “It is not in me, let <dn>Elohim</dn> answer <dn>את</dn> Pharaoh with peace.”
[17] And Pharaoh said to Yosěph, “See, in my dream I stood on the bank of the river
[18] and saw seven cows coming up out of the river, beautiful looking and fat, and they fed amongst the reeds,
[19] then saw seven other cows coming up after them, poor and very ugly and lean of flesh, such ugliness as I have never seen in all the land of Mitsrayim.
[20] “And the lean of flesh and ugly cows ate up <dn>את</dn> the first seven, the fat cows.
[21] “Yet when they had eaten them up, no one would have known that they had eaten them, for they were as ugly as at the beginning. Then I awoke.
[22] “Also, I looked in my dream and saw seven heads coming up on one stalk, complete and good,
[23] then saw seven heads, withered, lean, scorched by the east wind, coming up after them.
[24] “And the lean heads swallowed <dn>את</dn> the seven good heads. And I spoke to the magicians, but there was no one who could explain it to me.”
[25] And Yosěph said to Pharaoh, “The dream of Pharaoh is one. <dn>Elohim</dn> has shown Pharaoh <dn>את</dn> what <dn>He</dn> is about to do:
[26] “The seven good cows are seven years, and the seven good heads are seven years – it is one dream.
[27] “And the seven lean and ugly cows which came up after them are seven years, and the seven empty heads scorched by the east wind are seven years of scarcity of food.
[28] “This is the word which I spoke to Pharaoh: <dn>Elohim</dn> has shown <dn>את</dn> Pharaoh what <dn>He</dn> is about to do.
[29] “See, seven years of great plenty are coming in all the land of Mitsrayim,
[30] but after them seven years of scarcity of food shall arise and all the plenty be forgotten in the land of Mitsrayim. And the scarcity of food shall destroy <dn>את</dn> the land,
[31] and the plenty shall not be remembered in the land, because of the scarcity of food following, for it is very severe.
[32] “And the dream was repeated to Pharaoh twice because the word is established by <dn>Elohim</dn>, and <dn>Elohim</dn> is hastening to do it.
[33] “And now, let Pharaoh look for a discerning and wise man, and set him over the land of Mitsrayim.
[34] “Let Pharaoh do this, and let him appoint overseers over the land, to take up one-fifth of <dn>את</dn> the land of Mitsrayim in the seven years of plenty.
[35] “And let them gather <dn>את</dn> all the food of those good years that are coming, and store up grain under the hand of Pharaoh, and let them keep food in the cities.
[36] “And the food shall be for a store for the land for the seven years of scarcity of food which shall be in the land of Mitsrayim, and do not let the land be cut off by the scarcity of food.”

readings.title: Ruler Over All Egypt
readings.subtitle: The Gathering of the Grain
readings.text:
[Genesis 41:37] And the word was good in the eyes of Pharaoh and in the eyes of all his servants.
[38] And Pharaoh said to his servants, “Could we find another like him, a man in whom is the Spirit of <dn>Elohim</dn>?”
[39] Then Pharaoh said to Yosěph, “Since <dn>Elohim</dn> has shown <dn>את</dn> you <dn>את</dn> all this, there is no one as discerning and wise as you.
[40] “Be over my house, you yourself, and at your mouth all my people shall kiss – only in the throne I am greater than you.”
[41] And Pharaoh said to Yosěph, “See, I have set <dn>את</dn> you over all the land of Mitsrayim.”
[42] And Pharaoh took <dn>את</dn> his seal-ring off his hand and put <dn>את</dn> it on Yosěph’s hand. And he dressed <dn>את</dn> him in garments of fine linen and put a gold chain around his neck.
[43] And he had <dn>את</dn> him ride in the second chariot which he had. And they cried out before him, “Bow the knee!” And he set <dn>את</dn> him over all the land of Mitsrayim.
[44] And Pharaoh said to Yosěph, “I am Pharaoh, and without a word from you let no man lift <dn>את</dn> his hand or <dn>את</dn> foot in all the land of Mitsrayim.”
[45] And Pharaoh called Yosěph’s name Zaphnath-Pa‛něaḥ. And he gave him as a wife <dn>את</dn> Asenath, the daughter of Poti-Pherah priest of On. And Yosěph went out over all the land of Mitsrayim.
[46] Now Yosěph was thirty years old when he stood before Pharaoh sovereign of Mitsrayim. And Yosěph went out from the presence of Pharaoh, and went throughout all the land of Mitsrayim.
[47] And in the seven years of plenty the ground brought forth generously.
[48] And he gathered <dn>את</dn> all the food of the seven years which were in the land of Mitsrayim, and laid up the food in the cities. He laid up in every city the food of the fields which surrounded them.
[49] Thus Yosěph gathered very much grain, as the sand of the sea, until he ceased counting, for it was without number.
[50] And to Yosěph were born two sons before the years of scarcity of food came, whom Asenath, the daughter of Poti-Pherah priest of On, bore to him.
[51] And Yosěph called <dn>את</dn> the name of the first-born Menashsheh, “For <dn>Elohim</dn> has made me forget <dn>את</dn> all my toil and <dn>את</dn> all my father’s house.”
[52] And <dn>את</dn> the name of the second he called Ephrayim, “For <dn>Elohim</dn> has caused me to be fruitful in the land of my affliction.”
[53] And the seven years of plenty which were in the land of Mitsrayim came to an end,
[54] and the seven years of scarcity of food began to come, as Yosěph had said. And the scarcity of food was in all lands, but in all the land of Mitsrayim there was bread.
[55] But when all the land of Mitsrayim hungered, and the people cried to Pharaoh for bread, Pharaoh said to all the Mitsrites, “Go to Yosěph, do whatever he says to you.”
[56] And the scarcity of food was over all the face of the earth, and Yosěph opened <dn>את</dn> all the storehouses and sold to the Mitsrites. And the scarcity of food was severe in the land of Mitsrayim.
[57] And all the earth came to Yosěph in Mitsrayim to buy grain, because the scarcity of food was severe in all the earth.
